scope: P1 native gateway bootstrap/standard-refresh use cases, not yet HTTP/DI or provider gateway
behaviors: Lost bootstrap response recovers the same encrypted pair after native refresh; operation receipts contain only head ID/version.
Four identical bootstraps recover one pair; four distinct initial operations produce one winner and three observed-version conflicts.
Expired/superseded bootstrap operation cannot create or replace a head; a new observed operation updates client build without replacing the device.
Four standard refresh requests serialize into one rotation and recover the same winning pair; the native session and device remain unchanged.
Expired gateway access can refresh with current native authority; expired previous refresh cannot revoke the winner.
Expired native HRIS access denies gateway refresh; ordinary native refresh permits the retained gateway/device to continue.
Both bootstrap replay and refresh recheck permission, voluntary MFA, minimum build, disabled module, revoked device and account security version.
Revocation after the unscoped token lookup but before guarded admission is rejected.
Failure after writes rolls back tokens, receipt, audit and outbox; a scheduled company-policy boundary also rolls back issuance.
Final response validation uses one instant for current admission and authenticated response lifetime; a live access token cannot extend an expired admission or replay.
limits: No HTTP endpoint/Matrix error mapper, status metadata, public provider proxy, DI or maintenance worker was added in this increment.
No Synapse bearer is issued to clients or Matrix E2EE key created by these use cases.
Provider tests from prior checkpoints remain distinct; these tests use real PostgreSQL with fictional HRIS identities and controlled activation.
No live stack, phone, Mobile or Starter change occurred.
